# SPE round 5 plan: invoice extraction (configs Q, R, S)

Nothing is written until you approve this plan. The streak of matched rounds is 0 because config R missed in r04, so round 5 cannot end the loop.

Defaults I chose for details missing from the prompt:
- Requirement IDs start at R40 as a stand-in. When I write `spe/spec/spec.md`, I will renumber them to continue from the last ID in that file.
- New grader checks use the names below. Existing r04 checks keep their names.

## Specify

### Proposals from r04

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt as config S | It targets r04 F9 directly. It is one change on top of config R. |
| P2 | Reject for r05. Logged as D-row in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` | Q measured 0.93, so Q is not at a ceiling. The 15 new invoices have no AP lead reference fields yet, and only you and the AP lead can supply them. A different eval set would break the comparison with r04 in the same round that tests P1. |
| P3 | Adopt | P trails Q on every r04 metric, and no r05 comparison needs P. P's r01 to r04 rows stay in the log with a retirement note. |

### Requirements (round 5)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R40 | Config S is config R plus one layout check. The check skips OCR cleanup for the whole invoice when any page has two columns. | r04 F9, P1 adopted | Dry run trace: S makes no cleanup call on the two-column invoice and does call cleanup on the scanned single-column invoice. `line_item_recall[layout=two_column]` for S falls inside its band. |
| R41 | S's layout check decides from the PDF alone. It never reads eval tags or reference fields. | Evaluative rule that the author does not touch the judge | Leak gate G3: a static check of S's prompt and tool code, plus a check of the harness mounts. |
| R42 | Each of the 60 invoices gets two grader-only tags, `layout` (one_column or two_column) and `scanned` (yes or no). They live in `spe/evals/data/r05-tags.csv`. | r04 F9 (the fix needs a slice to measure it) | The file has 60 rows and is committed before the dry run. The two-column list goes in the round report so you can correct it. |
| R43 | Report total accuracy on the scanned slice for Q, R, and S. | r04 prediction log: R's Why "OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals" broke and was never tested on its own | Grader check `total_match[scanned=yes]` |
| R44 | Retire config P. | P3 adopted | Workflow `configs` argument is `[Q, R, S]` |
| R45 | Keep the same 60 invoices and the same AP lead references as r04. | P2 rejected, comparability with r04 | Dataset hash matches r04 |

### Defaults for this round

| Item | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Keep config R | Rerun R unchanged | S minus R in the same run isolates the skip rule. |
| Skip scope | Per invoice, not per page | This is the smaller change. A per-page skip can be a later proposal. |
| Tagging | I tag from the PDFs before the dry run | Only the slice rows depend on the tags. You can correct the tags next round. |
| Trials per invoice, budget cap | Same as r04, read from `spe/plans/r04.md` | Nothing in r04 points to a change. |
| D-row for P2 | "Add 15 handwritten scanned invoices as a separate slice in r06?" Decides: you with the AP lead. Status: open. | A new slice needs reference fields first. |

## Predict

Each cell is a number with a band. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. Q and R are unchanged, so their overall row starts from the r04 measured values.

| Metric | Grader check | Q | R | S | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy, all 60 | `field_accuracy` | 0.93 ± 0.02 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | Q and R are unchanged from r04. S takes Q's path on two-column invoices, which removes the F9 loss. r04 showed no gain from cleanup elsewhere, so I predict none. |
| Line-item recall, two-column slice | `line_item_recall[layout=two_column]` | 0.92 ± 0.06 | 0.70 ± 0.15 | 0.92 ± 0.06 | F9 says cleanup drops line items on these invoices. Q and S both skip cleanup here, so they should match. These are first slice estimates, so the bands are wide. |
| Total accuracy, scanned slice | `total_match[scanned=yes]` | 0.90 ± 0.08 | 0.90 ± 0.08 | 0.90 ± 0.08 | No measurement backs R's claim about scanned totals, so I predict no difference. If R and S beat Q here, the cleanup helps. |
| Layout check agreement with tags | `layout_agreement` | n/a | n/a | 0.97 ± 0.03 | Only S has the check. A two-column layout is usually clear in the PDF text positions. |

Any other r04 metric rows, such as PO mismatch flags, carry into `r05.yaml` this way:
- Q and R take their r04 measured values with their r04 bands.
- S takes Q's value, for the same reason as the first row.
- I will list these rows in `spe/plans/r05.md` before the commit.

The naive column follows the same rule the log used in r04.

## Evaluate

### After approval, in order
1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` from the Predict table. That file is never edited after a trial runs.
2. Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md` with your pasted text and "go again" word for word. Add the r05 table to `spe/spec/spec.md`, with P retired and a note. Add the P2 D-row to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
3. Commit locally: `spe r05 specify: respec from r04 F9, adopt P1 and P3, defer P2`.
4. Commit locally: `spe r05 predict: plan and predictions for Q, R, S`.

### Gates (any failure halts and I report back)

| Gate | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| G0 Tags | `spe/evals/data/r05-tags.csv` has 60 rows. The agent configs cannot read it. |
| G1 Grader selftest | Gold fixtures score 1.0. A planted fixture with one dropped two-column line item scores lower on `line_item_recall`. The slice filters return the expected rows. |
| G2 Control regrade of r04 | The current grader rescores the stored r04 outputs at Q 0.93 and R 0.88, each within 0.005. The r04 slice scores go in the log as background only. They do not change `r05.yaml`. |
| G3 Leak check | S's prompt and tool code do not reference tags or reference fields. The harness does not mount either path for the agent. |
| G4 Dry run | Two invoices (one two-column, one scanned single-column) run on each of Q, R, and S. Outputs parse to the schema. S's trace shows a skip on the first invoice and a cleanup call on the second. No scores are reported. |

### Workflow launch

```
script: spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js   (copy of r04 script, three changes: configs, S definition, slice checks)
args:
  round: 5
  configs: [Q, R, S]
  model: Sonnet 5.5
  dataset: r04 dataset path, hash checked against r04
  tags: spe/evals/data/r05-tags.csv   (grader only)
  trials_per_invoice: same as r04
  budget_cap: same as r04
  predictions: spe/predictions/r05.yaml
  checks: [field_accuracy, line_item_recall, total_match, layout_agreement, plus the r04 checks]
  out: spe/evals/results/r05/
```

### Cost (unmeasured estimate)
- The run has the same number of agent runs as r04, which is 3 configs × 60 invoices × the r04 trial count.
- S adds one layout check per invoice. The dry run adds 6 runs.
- I expect about the r04 cost plus 5%. If the budget cap is reached, the run halts and I report.

### After the run
1. Commit locally: `spe r05 evaluate: results for Q, R, S`.
2. Learn step:
   - Add the r05 rows to `spe/prediction-log.md` with predicted, measured, naive, and hit or miss.
   - Close F9 in `spe/failures.md` if S's two-column slice matches Q. Otherwise open F10 and say whether the layout check or the cleanup caused it.
   - Leave a "Proposed for round 6" table that includes P2, pending its D-row.
3. Commit locally: `spe r05 learn: close-out and r06 proposals`.

I do not push, deploy, or send anything.
